definition: Shogun is a free, open-source machine learning software library written in C++.
details: It offers numerous algorithms and data structures for machine learning problems. It offers interfaces for Octave, Python, R, Java, Lua, Ruby and C# using SWIG. It is licensed under the terms of the GNU General Public License version 3 or later.

explainer.lead: Shogun is a free, open-source machine learning software library written in C++ that provides numerous algorithms and data structures. It matters as a broad, openly licensed toolkit usable from many languages.

tiers.eli5: It's a big free toolbox of machine learning tools that programmers can use from several different languages.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers call its algorithms from C++ or from interfaces for Octave, Python, R, Java, Lua, Ruby and C# via SWIG. A pitfall is that its licence terms affect how it can be distributed and used in products.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition applies; it is a software library licensed under the GNU General Public License version 3 or later. Its limits are those of a general-purpose library rather than a theoretical method.

explainer.example: A team writes Python code that calls Shogun's C++ algorithms through its SWIG-generated interface.
